tg.name: Cateran Trail
tg.description: Blairgowrie

tg.name: Two Forts Trail
tg.description: Visits Moncreiffe Hill and Moredun Top Hillforts. Good paths with some steep inclines.

tg.name: Three Saints Way
tg.description: Three Saints Way – Killin to St Andrews. The lives of three saints – Saint Kessog, Saint Fillan and Saint Serf – are commemorated by this pilgrimage, connecting Scotland’s dramatic west coast to the rocks and hills of the east.

tg.name: Raven Trail
tg.description: Get a bird's eye view from the open slopes of Balkello Hill, which has a sweeping vista over Dundee and the Angus coast.

tg.name: Woodland Wander
tg.description: Wind your way through the young woodland. The native trees growing here are becoming a great home for wildlife.

tg.name: Sidlaws View Trail
tg.description: Enjoy the panorama of Balkello Hill, Auchterhouse Hill and Balluderon Hill from this gentle trail through the trees.

tg.name: Aaron's Walk
tg.description: A route that takes in the historical sites around Abernethy but with minimal stretches on road. It was suggested by walking group regular Aaron who comes from Abernethy. The first half is very easy and flat. The second half involves steep hill climbs.

tg.name: Bridge of Earn to Abernethy
tg.description: Good track to bridge at Culfargie then tricky navigation around solar farm, then good tracks again.

tg.name: Deuchny Trail
tg.description: Follow in the footsteps of ancient kings on this circuit of Deuchny Wood that has great views across the Perthshire countryside.

tg.name: Corsiehill Trail
tg.description: A circuit of the deciduous wooded slopes of Kinnoull Hill, with magnificent views from the summit over Perth and the Tay Valley.

tg.name: Barnhill Trail
tg.description: Climb straight out of Perth through beautifully varied woodland to the majestic summit of Kinnoull Hill.

tg.name: Tower Trail
tg.description: Climb Kinnoull Hill via the Earl's romantic tower, perched on the cliff edge with fabulous views over the Tay Valley.

tg.name: Jubilee Trail
tg.description: Experience the charms of Kinnoull Hill without climing to the summit on this short loop through varied pine, beech and spruce forest that is alive with birdsong.
tg.note: Yes, the typo on "climing" is accurate.

tg.name: Abernethy to Newburgh
tg.description: Following A913 but there is a footpath at the side of the road.

tg.name: Columba Way on North FCP
tg.description: Entirely on North section of Fife Coastal Path.

n: The Den and Kinpurney Tower Walk

tg.name: The Den and Kinpurney Tower Walk
Birnam Hill Path
tg.description: A popular walk requiring hill fitness as the north side path is of mountain hiking grade. The ascent is worthwhile for fabulous views from this commanding peak near the Highland Boundary Fault. To the south lies gentler landscape towards Perth and Strathe

tg.name: Loch of the Lowes Path
tg.description: Joins Dunkeld with Loch of the Lowes Nature Reserve in a loop. Pleasant woodland walk. Some muddy sections near Fungarth.

tg.name: Birnam Riverside Path
tg.description: Walk beside the River Tay passing the Birnam Oak. Goes downstream past the water treatment works before turning at the Fisherman's Hut. Returns through Birnam.

tg.name: Inver Path
tg.description: A short but steep section at the north end may be challenging. Otherwise a great combination of riverside and forest.

tg.name: Braan Path
tg.description: A stunning walk taking in the Hermitage and Rumbling Bridge waterfalls, along with stunning native woodland near Tomgarrow. Note that shortcutting along the A822 is hazardous and not recommended.

tg.name: Corbenic Poetry Path
tg.description: The Corbenic Poetry Path meanders through a variety of terrains including open hillside, moorland, ancient native woodlands, hazel coppice, and riverbanks. The path has been designed with a variety of surfaces to be as sensitive as possible to the environ

tg.name: Dunmore Trail
tg.description: Circuit of picturesque Dunmore Loch, mainly flat with some short, gentle inclines. Path surface is firm, fine gravel.

tg.name: Fiddler's Path
tg.description: Beautiful riverside path which is mostly hiking grade however there is a short section of steep uneven ground. There are tree roots and trunks to step over.
tg.note: The footbridge over the Braan washed away October 2023. The route has been updated to use the road bridge into Inver. It is possible to cross the Braan at the A9 on a footway - this uses a steep section of embankment.

tg.name: Faskally Forest 5km ParkRun Route
tg.description: This is the route used by the Faskally Forest Parkrun. Follow spur to join loop. Three laps. Return along spur from the loop. Trail - terrain is firm path or needle-leaved forest floor. Ok in trainers with good grip.

tg.name: Atholl Woods Path
tg.description: Includes a short section on road. An open-sided boat shed at Mill Dam provides shelter if required.

tg.name: Clachan Trail
tg.description: Mostly wide, firm gravel surface. Uneven grassy section with some muddy patches. Includes some fairly steep slopes. Look out for vehicles along well-used forest roads.

tg.name: Inchewan Path
tg.description: A lollipop route through the enclosed Inchewan Glen gorge before a loop in open country at at Balhomish and native woodland near Tomgarrow.

tg.name: Ring Fort Trail
tg.description: Firm gravel surface throughout with some uneven and slightly grassed over sections. One long steep slope. Includes a section along a well-used forest road.

n: The Duchess and the Bishop's Walk

tg.name: The Duchess and the Bishop's Walk
tg.description: A leisurely walk with one small section of steps and gentle inclines. The walk uses the Bishop's Path and Connects with the little know but very picturesque Duchess Bridle Path to reach Dunkeld House Hotel. It then returns via the side of the River Tay.

tg.name: The Strathbraan Pilgrims' Path
tg.description: Route may be muddy but terrain and gradients are gentle. Some streams are forded - boots required S of River Braan. Path indistinct in sections. Care is needed on road sections, particularly A822.
tg.via: Ballinreigh (former settlement);Glenfender;Dalreoch;Wester Dullator (former settlement);Dullator;Aldmad;Little Findowie (former settlement);Meikle Findowie;Drumour Steading;Corbenic Poetry Path;Ballinloan;Ballinlick;Meikle Logie;Lagganallachy;Kennacoil

tg.name: Weem Forest Trail
tg.description: Short but with steep sections and steps, with drops.

tg.name: Torryvald Route
tg.description: Easy woodland walk on good surface (some gradients and a short, flat section with some tree roots). There are frequent marker posts with yellow stripe. The Torryvald Folly is at the highpoint of the path.

tg.name: Bertha Loch Loop from Pitcairngreen
tg.description: A boots plod through mature woodland with views of Bertha Loch. This is an adventurous local ramble. Can be overgrown with ferns in summer.

tg.name: Pine Cone Point Path
tg.description: Pleasant out-and-back woodland route on firm path to Pine Cone Point viewpoint. The zig-zag climbing section ascends approximately 100 metres.

tg.name: Duchess Cave and Cave Crag
tg.description: Adventurous route to see the Duchess Cave, Waterfall and the famous Cave Crag climbing location. Requires sure-footedness and sturdy footwear. Ideal for fit and adventurous children.

tg.name: Loch A Choire Route
tg.description: Route up to Loch beneath Ben Vrackie. Mostly hiking grade with some mountain hiking beyond Loch A Choire

tg.name: Glen Garr Path
tg.description: Mostly good path but boggy in places and liable to fern cover in summer. Gentle gradients.

tg.name: Dunkeld Christmas Grotto Walk
tg.description: Dunkeld Christmas Eve Grotto Walk visits the cave. There are sections of the route that are on narrow uneven paths (mountain hiking). These sections may be bypassed. Most of the route is hiking.

tg.name: Feldy Roo Fitness Trail
tg.description: A three loop 5k walk,jog or run route. Suitable for rugged wheelchairs and strollers. Loop is 1.68km/1 mile

tg.name: Civil Engineering Walk
tg.description: A route that has several transport engineering points of interest involving historic hydro, road and rail infrastructure yet also has beautiful scenery. Grade is hiking but with short sections with uneven pathways.

tg.name: Rocking Stone Path
tg.description: Narrow, uneven, cambered paths with steep drops in places. Views from Polney Crag and the Rocking Stone - a glacial artefact.

tg.name: Deuchary Hill from Dunkeld
tg.description: The final ascent is steep demanding mountain hiking but most of this route is tracks with no extreme inclines.

n: Birnam Hill and The River Tay

tg.name: Birnam Hill and The River Tay
tg.description: An adventurous route over Birnam Hill, through where the buffalo roamed and back along the River Tay

tg.name: Castle Dow Hill Fort
tg.description: Good tracks but a stiff climb. Take care not to miss the junction that takes you to the fort. Great views of Strathtay and the north from the fort.

tg.name: Dalguise to Dunkeld
tg.description: Forestry trails with gradual inclines.

tg.name: Station to the Hermitage
tg.description: Arriving by train to Dunkeld and Birnam, a visit to the Hermitage is highly recommended. Please use this route avoiding the A9 (which is unsuitable for pedestrians). Say hello to Niel Gow's statue and pass through his birthplace, Inver.

tg.name: Cally Loch and Hatton Circular
tg.description: Uses old tracks, muddy in places and with the occasional fallen tree to cross.

tg.name: River Tay Way
tg.description: This is a newly proposed route.

tg.name: Luncarty Stanley River Walk
tg.description: Mostly following the former mill lade from the weir at Stanley, near Thistlebridge Rapids, that flowed to the bleaching mills at Luncarty. Experienced walkers only. Avoids busy roads without footpaths.

n: Duchess Cave from Cally Car Park

tg.name: Duchess Cave from Cally Car Park
tg.description: Micro-adventure route that requires good balance and clambering over obstacles

n: Hermitage, Rumbling Bridge and Inchewan Burn

tg.name: Hermitage, Rumbling Bridge and Inchewan Burn
tg.description: Walk that combines parts of the Braan Path and the Inchewan Path to make a loop form Dunkeld

tg.name: Duchess Anne to Kings Seat
tg.description: Directions to King's Seat Pictish Hill Fort from Dunkeld Community Archive. The final part of this walk is in steep terrain and is for experienced hikers only. If in doubt, employ a guide.

tg.name: Craigower Viewpoint
tg.description: A challenging climb followed by a gradual descent makes this ideal for a headtorch night walk. Refreshments at the Golf Club afterwards

tg.name: Buffalo Hut
tg.description: Pleasant walk with fine views south towards lowland Perthshire at this vantage point at the threshold of Highland Perthshire.

n: Diversion for Cathedral Path Repairs December 05

tg.name: Diversion for Cathedral Path Repairs December 05
tg.description: Alternative route whilst path repairs scheduled for the 8-10 December 2025  are underway. The voids the muddy field.

tg.name: Newton Bridge to Dallick
tg.description: Walkable route respecting curtilage at Dallick. Tracks with a few wet sections. Care needed if livestock in fields.

tg.name: Newton Bridge to Amulree
tg.description: Mostly off road, parts are boggy.

tg.name: Birks of Aberfeldy Walk
tg.description: Follows  the Moness Burn up up and then back down the other side.

tg.name: Perth to Bridge of Earn
tg.description: Separate footway alongside main road, share in part with cycles

tg.name: Dunkeld to Scone
tg.description: A sorter, more direct route than River Tay Trail. Boots required and ability to read a map.

tg.name: Scone to Perth
tg.description: Uses footpaths alongside the road and then across the Tay to St Johns Kirk

tg.name: Butterstone Dunkeld Circular
tg.description: Good tracks and quiet roads

tg.name: Comrie Croft to Crieff
tg.description: Mostly following the River Earn

tg.name: Crieff to Dallick
tg.description: Partly on old military road with some short tricky sections

tg.name: Sculpture Trail
tg.description: Visitors can enjoy following The Sculpture Trail, which includes a mixture of contemporary and 18th-century sculpture, through the castle gardens and grounds.

tg.name: Coillebrochain and Linn of Tummel
tg.description: Coillebrachan is were Robert Bruce rested after the battle of Methven. Ruins are not much to look at but the walk is beautiful

tg.name: Comrie to Comrie Croft
tg.description: Meanders through woods away from the busy A85
